name: Candela laser

lead: Candela makes aesthetic laser systems, and in looksmaxxing talk "Candela laser" stands for the clinic machines it sells, such as the GentleMax Pro and the PicoWay. People pick the device that matches the concern: hair, pigment, redness or tattoos.

Different systems use different wavelengths: alexandrite and Nd:YAG for hair and pigment, pulsed dye for blood vessels, and picosecond pulses for pigment and tattoos. Registered studies name its products, including a 1064-nm skin-tightening system and a 595 nm pulsed-dye laser. Research is device by device rather than for the brand as a whole.

paras: These are professional devices used in dermatology and aesthetic clinics. Most treatments are done in a series of sessions, and the right platform depends on the goal and the person's skin type.
Risks depend on the device and skin type and can include redness, pigment changes and burns. These are clinic-only devices, and operator choice and settings affect outcomes.

angle.text: "Candela laser" refers to a family of clinic laser platforms used for hair removal, pigment, redness and tattoos, so users pick the device that matches their concern and get clearer, smoother skin. Evidence exists per device rather than for the brand overall.

lead: Candela is the name of a manufacturer of aesthetic laser systems, and in looksmaxxing discussion "Candela laser" refers to the clinic platforms sold under that brand rather than a single machine. Registered studies name its products including the GentleMax Pro (alexandrite plus Nd:YAG), a 1064-nm Nd:YAG skin-tightening system, a pulsed-dye (595 nm) laser and the PicoWay picosecond system.[1][2][3]

These platforms are used in clinics for hair reduction, tattoo removal, wrinkles, acne, pigmented lesions and vascular birthmarks such as port-wine stains, according to the conditions listed in registered evaluations.[1][4] Evidence is spread across many device-specific studies and is not a single body of work. This entry is distinct from the SI unit of luminous intensity of the same name.

paras: A 500-participant evaluation of Candela technology, started in 2023, lists hair reduction, tattoo removal, wrinkles and acne as conditions.[1] Other registered studies name a 1064-nm Nd:YAG laser for skin tightening (22 participants, started 2006)[2], the PicoWay picosecond system for wrinkles and pigmented lesions (50 participants, started 2020)[3], and the GentleMax Pro for hair and pigmented and vascular lesions. Candela pulsed dye lasers are used with cooling for vascular conditions, and registered studies have examined them for port-wine stain and cutaneous lupus.[4][5]

Registered studies are small and mostly open-label. They include a pulsed dye laser combined with bipolar radiofrequency for port-wine stain (22 participants)[4], a 595-nm flashlamp pulsed dye laser for cutaneous lupus erythematosus (10 participants)[5], alexandrite laser for nevus flammeus (19 participants)[6], and a non-cutting laser in acne (44 participants).[7] A comparison of Q-switched alexandrite, Nd:YAG and ruby lasers on blue-black tattoos is also listed in the literature on laser tattoo treatment.[8] Results are not summarised in the registry entries cited here, and no single trial evaluates the brand as a whole.
The brand is mentioned as one of the clinic platforms (alongside others) that practices use for laser hair removal and skin procedures. No community discussion is summarised here.
